questions.prompt: What are conjunctions?
questions.explain: Conjunctions are joining words that connect words, phrases, or sentences.

questions.prompt: Conjunctions connect words, phrases, or ___.
questions.explain: Conjunctions connect words, phrases, or sentences.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, the letter F stands for ___.
questions.explain: F stands for For.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, the letter A stands for ___.
questions.explain: A stands for And.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, the letter N stands for ___.
questions.explain: N stands for Nor.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, what does the letter B stand for?
questions.explain: B stands for But.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, the letter O stands for ___.
questions.explain: O stands for Or.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, the letter Y stands for ___.
questions.explain: Y stands for Yet.

questions.prompt: In FANBOYS, what does the letter S stand for?
questions.explain: S stands for So.

questions.prompt: Which word is NOT one of the FANBOYS conjunctions?
questions.explain: Although is a subordinating conjunction, so it is not in FANBOYS.

questions.prompt: How many conjunctions are there in FANBOYS?
questions.explain: FANBOYS has seven letters: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So.

questions.prompt: Is 'nor' one of the FANBOYS conjunctions? (yes / no)
questions.explain: N in FANBOYS stands for Nor.

questions.prompt: Is 'because' one of the FANBOYS conjunctions? (yes / no)
questions.explain: FANBOYS is For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So, and because is not on the list.

questions.prompt: Coordinating conjunctions join two ideas that ___.
questions.explain: Coordinating conjunctions join two ideas that can stand on their own.

questions.prompt: Subordinating conjunctions connect a main idea to an idea that ___.
questions.explain: A subordinating conjunction connects a main idea to an idea that depends on it.

questions.prompt: Correlative conjunctions ___.
questions.explain: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs, like either ... or.

questions.prompt: In 'Beowulf and Wiglaf fought the dragon', the word 'and' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: And is one of the FANBOYS, so it is coordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'The sword was heavy, but Beowulf lifted it', the word 'but' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: But is one of the FANBOYS, so it is coordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'Do you want to attack or wait?', the word 'or' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Or is one of the FANBOYS, so it is coordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'Although he was old, the king fought', the word 'although' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Although introduces an idea that depends on the main idea, so it is subordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'I will play if it stops raining', the word 'if' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: If introduces a dependent idea, so it is subordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'Call me when you arrive', the word 'when' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: When introduces a dependent idea, so it is subordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'You can have either tea or coffee', the pair 'either ... or' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Either ... or works in a pair, so it is correlative.

questions.prompt: Complete the pair: Both the hero ___ his friend were brave.
questions.explain: Both is always paired with and.

questions.prompt: Complete the pair: Neither the king ___ the queen will speak.
questions.explain: Neither is always paired with nor.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction shows a reason?
questions.explain: Because introduces the reason for something.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction shows a result?
questions.explain: So introduces the result of something.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction shows a contrast?
questions.explain: Although introduces an idea that contrasts with the main idea.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction shows a choice?
questions.explain: Or links two possible choices.

questions.prompt: Beowulf fought Grendel ___ he wanted to protect the Danes.
questions.explain: Because introduces the reason he fought.

questions.prompt: The sword was heavy, ___ Beowulf lifted it easily.
questions.explain: But links two ideas that contrast.

questions.prompt: Grendel attacked every night, ___ the Danes could not sleep.
questions.explain: So introduces the result of the attacks.

questions.prompt: You can wear the red kit ___ the blue kit, but not both.
questions.explain: Or links two choices.

questions.prompt: The match will be cancelled ___ it rains.
questions.explain: If introduces a condition.

questions.prompt: Please call me ___ you arrive at the stadium.
questions.explain: When introduces the time of the action.

questions.prompt: We played well, ___ we lost the match.
questions.explain: But links two ideas that contrast.

questions.prompt: The pitch was wet, ___ the players kept slipping.
questions.explain: So introduces the result of the wet pitch.

questions.prompt: The referee stopped the game ___ a player was hurt.
questions.explain: Because gives the reason the game stopped.

questions.prompt: You can choose ___ the sword ___ the shield, but not both.
questions.explain: Either ... or links two choices.

questions.prompt: In 'The man did not fight, nor did he run', the word 'nor' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Nor is one of the FANBOYS, so it is coordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'The sword was old, yet it was sharp', the word 'yet' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Yet is one of the FANBOYS, so it is coordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'We will lose unless we defend better', the word 'unless' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Unless introduces a dependent idea, so it is subordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'Wiglaf watched while Beowulf fought', the word 'while' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: While introduces a dependent idea, so it is subordinating.

questions.prompt: In 'Both the knight and the squire are ready', the pair 'both ... and' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Both ... and works in a pair, so it is correlative.

questions.prompt: In 'She is not only fast but also strong', the pair 'not only ... but also' is a ___ conjunction. (coordinating / subordinating / correlative)
questions.explain: Not only ... but also works in a pair, so it is correlative.

questions.prompt: Is 'yet' one of the FANBOYS conjunctions? (yes / no)
questions.explain: Y in FANBOYS stands for Yet.

questions.prompt: Is 'while' one of the FANBOYS conjunctions? (yes / no)
questions.explain: While is a subordinating conjunction, so it is not in FANBOYS.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction means 'if not'?
questions.explain: Unless means if not.

questions.prompt: Unless it stops raining, we will stay home. = If it does ___ stop raining, we will stay home.
questions.explain: Unless means if not.

questions.prompt: In 'I stayed in because it rained', the word 'because' introduces the ___. (reason / result)
questions.explain: It rained is the reason; I stayed in is the result.

questions.prompt: In 'It rained, so I stayed in', the word 'so' introduces the ___. (reason / result)
questions.explain: Staying in is the result of the rain.

questions.prompt: Beowulf did not run away, ___ did he ask for help.
questions.explain: Nor joins two negative ideas, and the helping verb comes before the subject after it.

questions.prompt: Complete the pair: Either the king ___ the queen will speak first.
questions.explain: Either is always paired with or.

questions.prompt: Complete the pair: She is not only fast but ___ strong.
questions.explain: The pair is not only ... but also.

questions.prompt: ___ the sea was rough, the Geats sailed on.
questions.explain: Although shows that the Geats sailed in spite of the rough sea.

questions.prompt: We will lose the final ___ we defend better.
questions.explain: Unless means if not: we lose if we do not defend better.

questions.prompt: She has played football ___ she was six.
questions.explain: Since gives the starting point in time.

questions.prompt: ___ it was getting dark, the team went home.
questions.explain: Since gives the reason here: it was getting dark.

questions.prompt: Wiglaf watched ___ Beowulf fought the dragon.
questions.explain: While shows two things happening at the same time.

questions.prompt: Beowulf loved adventure, ___ Hrothgar preferred a quiet life.
questions.explain: While can show a contrast between two people.

questions.prompt: The hall was empty ___ everyone had left.
questions.explain: Because introduces the reason the hall was empty.

questions.prompt: Everyone had left, ___ the hall was empty.
questions.explain: So introduces the result of everyone leaving.

questions.prompt: The dragon woke up ___ the thief took a golden cup.
questions.explain: When shows the moment the dragon woke up.

questions.prompt: The goalkeeper was injured, ___ the coach chose a new one.
questions.explain: So introduces the result of the injury.

questions.prompt: You cannot join the team ___ you come to training.
questions.explain: Unless means if you do not come to training.

questions.prompt: Hrothgar was old, ___ he could not fight Grendel himself.
questions.explain: So introduces the result of being old.

questions.prompt: The warriors sang ___ the feast was going on.
questions.explain: While shows two things happening at the same time.

questions.prompt: The king will reward you ___ you defeat the monster.
questions.explain: If introduces the condition for the reward.

questions.prompt: The goalkeeper saved the penalty, ___ the team still lost.
questions.explain: But links two ideas that contrast.

questions.prompt: ___ Beowulf was exhausted, he refused to rest.
questions.explain: Although shows he refused to rest in spite of being exhausted.

questions.prompt: The match ended 0-0: ___ the home team ___ the visitors scored a goal.
questions.explain: Neither ... nor links two negative ideas.

questions.prompt: He is good at ___ running ___ swimming, so he enjoys both sports.
questions.explain: Both ... and links two things that are both true.

questions.prompt: The captain was ___ brave ___ very kind.
questions.explain: Not only ... but also adds a second quality.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses although correctly?
choices: Although it was late, the team kept training.
Although it was late, but the team kept training.
Although it was late, so the team kept training.
Although it was late, and the team kept training.
questions.answer: Although it was late, the team kept training.
questions.explain: Although is never used with but, so, or and in the same sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses because correctly?
choices: Because it rained, so we stayed inside.
Because it rained, but we stayed inside.
Because it rained, although we stayed inside.
Because it rained, we stayed inside.
questions.answer: Because it rained, we stayed inside.
questions.explain: Because is never used with so in the same sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means the same as 'You will not win unless you train'?
choices: If you train, you will not win.
You will win if you do not train.
If you do not train, you will not win.
You will not win because you train.
questions.answer: If you do not train, you will not win.
questions.explain: Unless means if not.

questions.prompt: I will tell you the news when I ___ home.
questions.explain: After when, we use the present simple to talk about the future.

questions.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
questions.explain: After if, we use the present simple to talk about the future.

questions.prompt: We will go to the beach tomorrow if the weather ___ nice.
questions.explain: After if, we use the present simple to talk about the future.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses when correctly to talk about the future?
choices: I will call you when I arrive.
I will call you when I will arrive.
I will call you when I would arrive.
I will call you when I arrived.
questions.answer: I will call you when I arrive.
questions.explain: After when, we use the present simple, not will, to talk about the future.

questions.prompt: Beowulf trusted his sword ___ it failed him against Grendel's mother.
questions.explain: Although shows a contrast: he trusted it, but it failed him.

questions.prompt: The Danes were frightened ___ Grendel was only one monster.
questions.explain: Although shows a contrast between their fear and the fact that he was only one monster.

questions.prompt: ___ the dragon sleeps, the village is safe.
questions.explain: While shows two things happening at the same time.

questions.prompt: ___ the knights were sleeping, the thief crept into the cave.
questions.explain: While shows that the two actions happened at the same time.

questions.prompt: You cannot enter the hall ___ you leave your sword outside.
questions.explain: Unless means if you do not leave your sword outside.

questions.prompt: In 'Since she was injured, she could not play', the word 'since' shows ___. (time / reason)
questions.explain: Here since means because.

questions.prompt: In 'I have known him since 2020', the word 'since' shows ___. (time / reason)
questions.explain: Here since gives a starting point in time.

questions.prompt: In 'While I was training, it started to rain', the word 'while' shows ___. (time / contrast)
questions.explain: Here while means at the same time as.

questions.prompt: In 'Beowulf is a warrior, while Hrothgar is a king', the word 'while' shows ___. (time / contrast)
questions.explain: Here while compares two different people.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses neither ... nor correctly?
choices: Neither the king nor the queen wasn't afraid.
Neither the king nor the queen was afraid.
Neither the king or the queen was afraid.
Neither the king and the queen was afraid.
questions.answer: Neither the king nor the queen was afraid.
questions.explain: Neither is paired with nor, and the pair already has a negative meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses both ... and correctly?
choices: Both the hero and his friend were brave.
Both the hero or his friend were brave.
Both the hero and his friend was brave.
Both the hero but his friend were brave.
questions.answer: Both the hero and his friend were brave.
questions.explain: Both ... and takes a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses either ... or correctly?
choices: Either you leave now nor you will miss the bus.
Either you leave now but you will miss the bus.
Either you leave now so you will miss the bus.
Either you leave now or you will miss the bus.
questions.answer: Either you leave now or you will miss the bus.
questions.explain: Either is paired with or.

questions.prompt: Which sentence puts the cause and the effect the right way round?
choices: It had rained because the ground was wet.
The ground was wet so it had rained.
The ground was wet because it had rained.
It had rained, so because the ground was wet.
questions.answer: The ground was wet because it had rained.
questions.explain: Because introduces the reason, and the rain is the reason for the wet ground.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the right word order after nor?
choices: Hrothgar did not sleep, nor he did rest.
Hrothgar did not sleep, nor did he rest.
Hrothgar did not sleep, nor did not he rest.
Hrothgar did not sleep, nor rested he not.
questions.answer: Hrothgar did not sleep, nor did he rest.
questions.explain: After nor, the helping verb comes before the subject.

questions.prompt: Both Beowulf and his men ___ ready to fight.
questions.explain: Both ... and takes a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Either the king or the queen ___ going to speak.
questions.explain: Both subjects are singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.prompt: Neither the dragon nor the wolf ___ afraid of fire.
questions.explain: Both subjects are singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.prompt: Neither the knights nor the soldiers ___ afraid of the monster.
questions.explain: Both subjects are plural, so the verb is plural.

questions.prompt: Either the players or the coaches ___ going to answer the questions.
questions.explain: Both subjects are plural, so the verb is plural.

questions.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? ___ Grendel ___ his mother could be beaten by ordinary men, so Beowulf was needed.
questions.explain: Neither ... nor links two negative ideas.

questions.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? Beowulf ___ fought Grendel ___ also his mother.
questions.explain: The pair is not only ... but also, and also is already in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? The hero was ___ strong ___ clever, so he won easily.
questions.explain: Both ... and links two qualities that are both true.

questions.prompt: Which pair completes the sentence? You must ___ train hard ___ accept losing, so choose now.
questions.explain: Either ... or links two options that exclude each other.
